known.intro:
What is limited or broken right now, and why. Worth reading before you report
something, because a lot of what looks like a bug is how a shared Skyrim has
to work.

Not all of it is permanent. The first group follows from SkyMP itself, and
none of it is settled for good. Everything after it is where things stand
today, and some of that is being worked on.

This table is being looked at.

sections.name: The load order rule
sections.note:
The server and every machine must carry the same plugins in the same order with the same bytes. The launcher compares every plugin's size and checksum with the server's list when it starts, and the game runs the same comparison at login. One machine out of step gets LOAD ORDER ERROR and cannot connect.

If the launcher says a plugin differs, press **Fix**. When it is Thornswood's own plugin, Fix downloads the server's copy and puts it in place, and **Scan** runs the comparison again. When it is another author's mod, the server does not hand it out: Scan and Fix name the mod, and updating the Thornswood collection or reinstalling that mod in Vortex puts it right.

If the game turns you away with LOAD ORDER ERROR, quit it and press **Scan**, then **Fix**. The launcher compares your order with the server's position by position, names the first place they differ, and Fix puts the server's order into this build's plugin list. That one downloads nothing. Do not play on and do not report anything else from that session: your machine is resolving objects to different things from everybody else's, so whatever you see next is not evidence.

Scan also sees the plugins the game loads on its own. Skyrim.ccc names the Creation Club content, and the game loads any of it that is sitting in Data whether or not a list asks for it, which puts everything after it out of step. Those are named too, and Fix moves them aside rather than deleting them.

This is why mods are added in batches rather than one at a time: every addition moves the load order for everybody at once.

archive.intro: Closed problems and their real causes. Kept for the causes, not the fixes.

sections.name: 14 September 2026
sections.note:
**Looting armour stripped worn gear.** The server validates every equipment change and rejects it if any two worn items claim the same body slot, unequipping all of them. Vanilla already uses slots 44 to 47 and cloak mods reach for the same free ones. Fixed by making the slot check a setting and turning it off. Searched for days on the client. The server had been logging the exact item IDs the whole time.
**World had no NPCs.** A hardcoded list in the server's C++ banned ten race IDs, which are the ten playable races, covering every human, elf, orc, khajiit and argonian. The NPC setting was already enabled. Fixed by moving the list into server settings and emptying it. The trace log named every skipped actor and the reason, and trace was never switched on.
**Enemy health mirrored your own.** The function reporting health ran once for your character and once per hosted NPC, but read values off your character every time. Fixed with an early return unless reporting your own character.
**Every door and chest unlocked.** Upstream unlocks every reference the server tracks, because it also blocks activation on containers, and locked plus blocked is unopenable by any means. Fixed by letting a locked reference keep its own handling until opened normally.
**Keyboard locked on load.** A browser focus flag blanks all keyboard reads. The bindings that raised it were removed, but another service still raised it and removing the bindings had deleted the only code that lowered it. Fixed by having Escape and menu open lower it again. Six wrong explanations, each shipped as a build. Alt tabbing out and back cured it, which was the clue, because leaving the process dropped the flag.
**Launcher would not reopen.** The launcher holds a single instance lock. Voice runs in a hidden window, and WPF closes an app when the last window closes, not the main one. Closing the launcher left the process alive holding the lock. Fixed by tying shutdown to the main window.
**Voice indicator stuck on LISTENING ONLY.** Audio moved to the launcher but the indicator still asked the game browser whether it had a microphone. The replacement request could fail silently because the error handler was empty. Fixed by pushing state in through the plugin, and the empty catch is gone.
**Load order check had never run.** The client asked a public master server that has never heard of this server, got a 404, and compared against an empty list, which passes. Fixed by having the server publish its own manifest. The yellow warning everyone ignored for weeks was that failed lookup.
**Server would not start after deploy.** Plugin paths in the server settings were written from the development machine and copied to the VPS, where the game lives elsewhere. The sync script takes the server path as an argument now.
**Start point pointed at the wrong mod.** The configured start point encodes a plugin's load order position. The order grew by two entries and the value was not updated. Must be rechecked whenever anything is added before Skyrim Unbound.
**Enchantment damage did nothing to anyone else.** The client accepted weapons, spells and scrolls as hit sources and dropped enchantments before reporting.

sections.name: Earlier, confirmed working
sections.note:
**Handles, levers and pull chains.** Blocked activation stopped the game running its own scripts on them, and the server has no scripts to run instead. Activators and furniture are no longer blocked.
**Voice chat.** The game's browser has no permission UI, an autoplay policy needing a click nobody can give, and a focus flag that takes the keyboard. Audio never worked there. Moved into the launcher, which is a real browser.

sections.name: 1. The door on the game server
sections.note: The biggest hole, and the one nothing else closes.

cells.s2a: **Anyone with the address can walk in**
cells.s2b:
There is no `sPassword` in server-settings.json, nothing in gamemode.js reads a password, and SkyMP has no join screen. The field only ever existed because the old multiplayer mod had one. So `192.135.112.23:7777` is open to any SkyMP client.

The launcher asking Discord does not fix this. That only stops people using your launcher. A stranger with a stock client goes straight past it.
cells.s2c:
**Today.** Firewall 7777 and 3000 to the addresses that should reach them. I can write it.

**Properly.** A check in gamemode.js on connect against the same ticket the site issues. That is the one that makes a ban bite.

cells.s2b: `Account.cs` posts to `http://` on every launch with the server password in the body. The password gates nothing, so this is disclosure rather than a way in, but it is the last plain HTTP left.
cells.s2c: Fixes itself when the register asks the site instead of the game server. Same work as the row above.

sections.name: 2. Taking the mods out of the installer
sections.note: Everything ships in the installer today: 21.5 GB staged, about 18 GB zipped, all of it required. This is the job that makes the installer small.

cells.s3b: A required core everybody must match byte for byte, because the load order check compares every plugin by name, size and crc32. Then optional packs on top, which are safe only because they contain no plugin at all: textures, meshes, weather, ENB, shaders.
cells.s3c: A pack with a plugin in it desyncs the server. Packaging has to refuse to build one, not trust me to remember.

cells.s3a: **The launcher already has half of it**
cells.s3b: `Updater.ApplyPack` downloads a zip, checks its SHA-256, and extracts `game\` and `profile\` trees. That is the install side, working today, used for updates.
cells.s3c: What is missing: a list of optional packs separate from the update packs, and a way to take one off again.

cells.s3a: **Removing a pack is not possible yet**
cells.s3b: Nothing records which files a pack wrote. `applied.txt` is one id per line, append only, no file list, no way to delete. And `ExtractToFile(full, true)` overwrites without keeping a copy, so Remove can restore emptiness but not what was there before.
cells.s3c: Needs: a per pack file list written at install time, and applied.txt rewritten rather than appended.

cells.s3a: **Pack has no name and no size**
cells.s3b: `Pack` in Config.cs is id, url, sha256, notes. A page listing packs has nothing to show for name or size.
cells.s3c: Two fields on Pack, and the publisher that writes version.json has to fill them.

What is being built and roughly in what order. Nothing here has a date on it, because a date would be a guess.

Things move up this list when somebody starts on them, not when they are announced.

G opens and closes it. Sixty emotes, eight quick slots in the middle of the wheel, a search and an alphabetical list beside it. Tab moves to the search while it is open, and N stops an emote you are stuck in. The number keys 1 to 8 play the slots with the wheel shut. The launcher's Controls page moves any of those keys
The towns keep the people they need: guild traders, drivers and the animals. Bethesda's guards, courts and wandering townsfolk are gone, so the people you meet are people
P on someone asks them, the P panel runs it, and the leader can kick, hand over the lead or disband. The party shows on a strip under the compass
When two people cannot connect directly, voice goes through the server's relay instead, so they still hear each other
Traders start with a purse and only have what people have spent with them. Prices come from a ledger, not from nowhere
The sky turns with the season, and crops do not grow in winter
Shared, ranked gathering. A fishery that needs a pole, traps, and rare seams that each sit in one place on their own clock
Chat is local and drawn above the speaker's head, with a voice mark, text mute and hidden names
